verses.1:1: And in the first year of Cyrus the king of the Persians, so that it might be fulfilled from the mouth of Jeremiah, He roused the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians, and he issued a proclamation in all his kingdom, and also in writing, saying,
verses.1:2: "Thus said Cyrus king of the Persians: The God of heaven has given me all the kingdoms, and He Himself has charged me to build a house for Him in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.
verses.1:3: Who among you is from all His people? And his God will be with him, and he will go up to Jerusalem.
verses.1:4: And as for everyone who remains from all the places where he resides, the men of his place will assist him with silver and gold and goods and livestock, along with the freewill offering for the house of the God who is in Jerusalem."
verses.1:5: And the leaders of the ancestral houses of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests, and the Levites rose up, all those whose spirit God roused to go up to build the house that is in Jerusalem.
verses.1:6: And all those around them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with goods, and with livestock, and with gifts, besides the freewill offerings.
verses.1:7: And King Cyrus brought out the vessels of the house, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem and placed in the house of his god.
verses.1:8: And Cyrus king of the Persians brought them out into the hand of Mithredath Tasbarenus, and he counted them out to Sabanasar, leader of Judah.
verses.1:9: And this is their number: for the Lord, thirty of gold and one thousand of silver, twenty-nine altered items,
verses.1:10: thirty bowls of gold and six of silver, and one thousand other vessels.
verses.1:11: All the vessels of gold and of silver were five thousand four hundred, all of them going up from the exile out of Babylon to Jerusalem.
verses.2:1: And these are the sons of the province who went up from the captivity of the exile that Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, deported to Babylon, and returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each man to his city.
verses.2:2: Those who came with Zerubbabel were Jeshua, Nehemiah, Araiah, Reelaiah, Marathchai, Baspham, Malsar, Batusi, Balleia. The number of the men of Israel:
verses.2:3: the sons of Perez, two thousand one hundred seventy-two;
verses.2:4: and the sons of Asaph, four hundred seventy-two;
verses.2:5: the sons of Era, seven hundred seventy-five;
verses.2:6: the sons of Phalab-moab, of the sons of Jeshua, Jobab, two thousand eight hundred twelve;
verses.2:7: the sons of Malam, one thousand two hundred fifty-four;
verses.2:8: the sons of Zattu, nine hundred forty-five;
verses.2:9: the sons of Zacchu, seven hundred sixty;
verses.2:10: the sons of Banu, six hundred forty-two;
verses.2:11: the sons of Bebai, six hundred twenty-three;
verses.2:12: the sons of Azgad, three thousand two hundred twenty-two;
verses.2:13: the sons of Adonikam, six hundred sixty-six;
verses.2:14: the sons of Baogei, two thousand fifty-six;
verses.2:15: the sons of Adin, four hundred fifty-four;
verses.2:16: the sons of Ater, of Hezekiah, ninety-two;
verses.2:17: the sons of Basu, three hundred twenty-three;
verses.2:18: the sons of Ura, one hundred twelve;
verses.2:19: the sons of Hashum, two hundred twenty-three;
verses.2:21: the sons of Barthaleem, one hundred twenty-three;
verses.2:23: the sons of Anathoth, one hundred twenty-eight;
verses.2:25: the sons of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred forty-three;
verses.2:26: the sons of Haram and Geba, six hundred twenty-one;
verses.2:27: the men of Michmash, one hundred twenty-two;
verses.2:28: the men of Gaithel and Ai, two hundred twenty-three;
verses.2:30: the sons of Magbish, one hundred fifty-six;
verses.2:31: the sons of Elamar, two thousand two hundred fifty-four;
verses.2:32: the sons of Harim, three hundred twenty;
verses.2:33: the sons of Lod, Haroth, and Ono, six hundred twenty-five;
verses.2:34: the sons of Jereia, three hundred forty-five;
verses.2:35: the sons of Senaah, three thousand six hundred thirty.
verses.2:36: And the priests: the sons of Jeuda, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred seventy-three;
verses.2:37: the sons of Immer, one thousand fifty-two;
verses.2:38: the sons of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred forty-seven;
verses.2:39: the sons of Harim, one thousand seven.
verses.2:40: And the Levites: the sons of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the sons of Soduiah, seventy-four;
verses.2:41: the singers: the sons of Asaph, one hundred forty-eight;
verses.2:42: the sons of the gates: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Akum, the sons of Hatita, the sons of Abau, in all, one hundred thirty-nine.
verses.2:43: The Nethinim: the sons of Suthia, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbaoth,
verses.2:44: the sons of Kadesh, the sons of Soel, the sons of Padon,
verses.2:45: the sons of Lebanah, the sons of Hagabah, the sons of Akaboth,
verses.2:46: the sons of Hagab, the sons of Samaan, the sons of Hanan,
verses.2:47: the sons of Keded, the sons of Gael, the sons of Reel,
verses.2:48: the sons of Rezin, the sons of Nekoda, the sons of Gazzam,
verses.2:49: the sons of Uzza, the sons of Phison, the sons of Besai,
verses.2:50: the sons of Asnah, the sons of Manoemin, the sons of Naphison,
verses.2:51: the sons of Bakbuk, the sons of Haphika, the sons of Harhur,
verses.2:52: the sons of Basadoe, the sons of Mauda, the sons of Harsha,
verses.2:53: the sons of Barkos, the sons of Temah,
verses.2:54: the sons of Nasus, the sons of Hatipha,
verses.2:55: the sons of Abdesel, the sons of Sotai, the sons of Hassophereth, the sons of Phadura,
verses.2:56: the sons of Jaalah, the sons of Darkon, the sons of Gedea,
verses.2:57: the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Hateia, the sons of Phasrath, the sons of Haseboin, the sons of Ami;
verses.2:58: all the Nethinim and the sons of Asedeselma, three hundred seventy-two.
verses.2:59: And these are the ones who went up from Thermeleth, Thaaresa, Charus, Addan, Immer; and they were not able to declare the house of their family and their seed, whether they were in Israel:
verses.2:60: the sons of Lachea, the sons of Bua, the sons of Tobiah, the sons of Nekoda, six hundred fifty-two.
verses.2:61: And from the sons of the priests: the sons of Labeia, the sons of Hakkoz, the sons of Zarbelthei, who took a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
verses.2:62: These searched for their written record, the Methoesim, and they were not found, and they were excluded from the priesthood.
verses.2:63: And Hathersaa said to them not to eat from the most holy things until a priest should arise with the lights and the perfections.
verses.2:64: Now the whole assembly was about forty-two thousand three hundred sixty,
verses.2:65: besides their servants, female servants; these were seven thousand three hundred thirty-four; and these were singers and songs, two hundred.
verses.2:66: Their horses were seven hundred thirty, and their mules were two hundred forty-five;
verses.2:67: their camels were four hundred thirty-five; their donkeys were seven hundred twenty.
verses.2:68: And some of the leaders of the families, when they came to the house of the Lord that is in Jerusalem, gave freewill offerings for the house of God to establish it on its prepared place.
verses.2:69: According to their ability, they gave into the treasury of the work pure gold, sixty-one thousand minas; and five thousand minas of silver; and one hundred tunics of the priests.
verses.2:70: And the priests, the Levites, some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the Thanieim settled in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.
verses.3:1: And the seventh month arrived, and the Israelites were in their cities, and the people were gathered together as one man to Jerusalem.
verses.3:2: And Jeshua the son of Jozadak and his brothers rose up, and they built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings on it, according to the things written in the law of Moses, the man of God.
verses.3:3: And they prepared the altar on its prepared base, and a burnt offering went up on it to the Lord in the morning and at evening.
verses.3:4: And they kept the feast of booths according to what is written, and offered burnt offerings day by day by number according to the ordinance, each day's requirement day by day;
verses.3:5: and after this, continual burnt offerings, and those for the new moons and for all the consecrated feasts, and for everyone who willingly offered a freewill offering to the Lord.
verses.3:6: On the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to the Lord; and the foundation of the house of the Lord had not been laid.
verses.3:7: And they gave silver to the stonecutters and to the carpenters, and food and drink and oil to the Sedamin and to the Sorin, to bring cedar timbers from Lebanon to the sea of Joppa, according to the permission of Cyrus king of the Persians for them.
verses.3:8: And in the second year of their coming to the house of God, to Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and Jeshua the son of Jozadak and the rest of the brothers, the priests and the Levites, and all those coming from the captivity to Jerusalem made a beginning, and they appointed the Levites from twenty years old and upward over the works of the Lord.
verses.3:9: And Jeshua and his sons and his brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, stood over those doing the works in the house of God; the sons of Henadad, their sons and their brothers, the Levites.
verses.3:10: And they laid the foundation to build the house of the Lord; and the priests stood robed with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, to praise the Lord by the hands of David king of Israel.
verses.3:11: And they responded in praise and thanksgiving to the Lord: "For it is good, for His mercy is forever upon Israel." And all the people sounded a loud shout to praise the Lord at the laying of the foundation of the house of the Lord.
verses.3:12: And many of the priests and the Levites and leaders of the fathers' houses, the older men who had seen the first house on its foundation, and this house before their eyes, were weeping with a loud voice, and a crowd was shouting with gladness to lift up a song.
verses.3:13: And the people did not distinguish the sound of the shouting of gladness from the sound of the weeping, for the people cried out with a loud voice, and it was heard even from afar.
verses.4:1: And those afflicting Judah and Benjamin heard that the sons of the exile were building a house for the Lord God of Israel;
verses.4:2: and they approached Zerubbabel and the leaders of the fathers' houses and said to them, "We will build with you, for like you we seek our God, and to Him we have been sacrificing from the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us here."
verses.4:3: And Zerubbabel and Jeshua and the rest of the leaders of the fathers' houses of Israel said to them, "It is not for us and for you to build a house for our God, for we together will build for the Lord our God, as Cyrus king of the Persians commanded us."
verses.4:4: And the people of the land were weakening the hands of the people of Judah, and they were hindering them from building,
verses.4:5: and hiring people against them, wanting to frustrate their plan, all the days of Cyrus king of the Persians and until the reign of Darius king of the Persians.
verses.4:6: And in the reign of Astherus, at the beginning of his reign, he wrote against those inhabiting Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.4:7: And in the days of Artaxerxes, he wrote in peace to Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of the fellow servants; to the king of the Persians the tax collector wrote a document in Aramaic and translated.
verses.4:8: Raul Badatamen and Shimshai the scribe wrote one letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes.
verses.4:9: Thus decided Rehum Baal and Shimshai the scribe and the rest of our fellow servants, the Dinaites, the Pharesthachites, the Taraphallites, the Aphrasites, the Archuites, the Babylonians, the Susynachites, who are Elamites,
verses.4:10: and the rest of the nations whom Osnappar the great and honorable deported and settled in the cities of Samaria, and the rest beyond the River.
verses.4:11: This is the copy of the letter that they sent to him: "To King Artaxerxes: your servants, the men beyond the River.
verses.4:12: Let it be known to the king that the Jews who went up from Cyrus to us have come to Jerusalem; they are building the rebellious and wicked city, and they have finished its walls and raised up its foundations.
verses.4:13: Now therefore let it be known to the king that if that city is built and its walls are finished, there will be no taxes for you, nor will they give any; and this harms kings.
verses.4:14: And it is not right for us to see the dishonor of the king; for this reason we have sent and made this known to the king,
verses.4:15: so that he may search in the book of records of your fathers, and you will find and know that that city is a rebellious city, harming kings and provinces, and that places of refuge for slaves have been in its midst from days of old; because of these things this city was laid waste.
verses.4:16: We make it known to the king that if that city is built and its walls are finished, you have no peace."
verses.4:17: And the king sent peace and a statement to Rehum Balgam and Shimshai the scribe and the rest of their fellow servants living in Samaria and the rest beyond the River:
verses.4:18: "The tax collector whom you sent to us was summoned before me.
verses.4:19: And a decree was issued by me, and we searched and found that that city from days of old rises up against kings, and rebellions and places of refuge arise in it;
verses.4:20: and mighty kings arise over Jerusalem, ruling over all the west of the River, and full taxes and a portion are given to them.
verses.4:21: Now issue a decree to stop those men, and that city will not be built anymore because of the decree.
verses.4:22: Be on guard against showing slackness concerning this, so that destruction may never increase to the harm of kings."
verses.4:23: Then the tax collector of King Artaxerxes read aloud before Rehum and Shimshai the scribe, their fellow servants; and they went in haste to Jerusalem and in Judah, and stopped them with horses and force.
verses.4:24: Then the work of the house of God that is in Jerusalem ceased, and it remained at a standstill until the second year of Darius the king of the Persians.
verses.5:1: And Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo prophesied a prophecy to the Jews who were in Judah and Jerusalem, in the name of the God of Israel over them.
verses.5:2: Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and Jeshua the son of Jozadak rose up and began to build the house of God that is in Jerusalem, and with them were the prophets of God, helping them.
verses.5:3: At that very time Tattenai, governor beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and their fellow servants came to them and said such things to them: "Who issued you a decree to build the house and to finish this outfitting?"
verses.5:4: Then they said these things to them: "What are the names of the men who are building this city?"
verses.5:5: And the eyes of God were upon the captivity of Judah, and they did not stop them until a report was brought to Darius; and then it was sent to the tax collector concerning this.
verses.5:6: The copy of the letter that Tattenai, governor of the region beyond, and Shethar-bozenai and their fellow servants, the Apharsachites beyond the River, sent to King Darius;
verses.5:7: they sent a report to him, and these things were written in it:
verses.5:8: "To King Darius, all peace. Let it be known to the king that we went to the province of Judea, to the house of the great God, and it is being built with choice stones, and timbers are being placed in the walls, and that work is being skillfully done and is prospering in their hands.
verses.5:9: Then we asked those elders and spoke to them like this: 'Who issued you a decree to build this outfitting and to finish it?'
verses.5:10: And we asked them their names to make them known to you, so as to write down the names of the men who were their leaders.
verses.5:11: And they answered us with this word, saying, 'We are servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are building the house that had been built many years before this, and a great king of Israel built it and finished it for them.
verses.5:12: But after our fathers provoked the God of heaven to anger, He gave them into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he destroyed this house and deported the people to Babylon.
verses.5:13: However, in the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus issued a decree that this house of God be built.
verses.5:14: And the silver and gold vessels of God, which Nebuchadnezzar brought out from the house that is in Jerusalem and carried away to the temple of the king, he gave to Bagasar the treasurer, who was over the treasury,
verses.5:15: and he said to him, "Take all the vessels; go, put them in the house that is in Jerusalem, in their own place."
verses.5:16: Then that Sarbagar came and laid the foundations of the house of God that is in Jerusalem; and from that time until now it has been built, and it has not been finished.'
verses.5:17: And now, if it is good to the king, let a search be made in the treasure house of the king of Babylon, so that you may know that a decree came from King Cyrus to build that house of God that is in Jerusalem; and when the king knows concerning this, let him send to us."
verses.6:1: Then King Darius issued a decree, and he searched in the archives where the treasury lies in Babylon.
verses.6:2: And there was found in the city, in the citadel, one scroll, and this memorandum was written in it:
verses.6:3: "In the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus issued a decree concerning the sacred house of God that is in Jerusalem and the place where they offer the sacrifices. And he set an elevation sixty cubits in height,
verses.6:4: and three courses of stone and one course of timber; and the expense will be given from the house of the king.
verses.6:5: And the silver and gold vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar brought out from the house that is in Jerusalem, were set in place in the house of God."
verses.6:6: "Now you will give, governors beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and their fellow servants, the Apharsachites beyond the River, keeping far from there;
verses.6:7: leave alone the work of the house of God; and let the elders of the Jews build that house of God in its place.
verses.6:8: And a decree has been issued by me that you never do anything with the elders of the Jews for the building of that house of God; and from the possessions of the king, from the tributes beyond the River, let the expense be diligently given to those men, so that it may not be stopped;
verses.6:9: and whatever is lacking, both young of cattle and of rams, and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, wheat, salt, wine, oil, according to the word of the priests who are in Jerusalem, let it be given to them day by day, whatever they ask,
verses.6:10: so that they may be offering pleasing aromas to the God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king and of his sons.
verses.6:11: And a decree has been issued by me that any person who alters this word, a beam will be pulled down from his house, and being set upright, he will be struck upon it, and his house will be made what belongs to me.
verses.6:12: And the God whose name dwells there will overthrow every king and people who stretches out his hand to alter or to destroy the house of God that is in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued a decree; it will be done diligently."
verses.6:13: Then Tattenai, governor beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and his fellow servants, according to what King Darius sent, did so diligently.
verses.6:14: And the elders of the Jews and the Levites were building through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo; and they built and completed it by the decree of the God of Israel and by the decree of Cyrus and Darius and Artaxerxes, kings of the Persians.
verses.6:15: And they finished this house by the third day of the month of Adar, which is the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.
verses.6:16: And the sons of Israel, the priests and the Levites and the rest of the sons of the exile, celebrated the dedication of the house of God with joy.
verses.6:17: And they offered for the dedication of the house of God one hundred young bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs; twelve male goats for a sin offering on behalf of all Israel, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
verses.6:18: And they appointed the priests in their division and the Levites in their portions for the service of God who is in Jerusalem, according to the writing of the book of Moses.
verses.6:19: And the sons of the exile celebrated the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
verses.6:20: For the priests and the Levites had purified themselves; to a single one, all were pure. And they slaughtered the Passover for all the sons of the exile, and for their brothers the priests, and for themselves.
verses.6:21: And the sons of Israel, from the exile, ate the Passover, and everyone separating himself to them with regard to the impurities of the nations of the land, to seek the Lord, the God of Israel.
verses.6:22: And they celebrated the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days with joy, because He made them joyful, and the heart of the king of Assyria turned toward them to strengthen their hands in the works of the house of the God of Israel.
verses.7:1: And after the events, in the reign of Artaxerxes, king of the Persians, Ezra went up, the son of Seraiah, the son of Azariah, the son of Hilkiah,
verses.7:2: the son of Shallum, the son of Zadok, the son of Ahitub,
verses.7:3: the son of Samariah, the son of Azariah, the son of Meraioth,
verses.7:4: the son of Zerahiah, the son of Saouia, the son of Bukki,
verses.7:5: the son of Abishua, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, the ancestral priest.
verses.7:6: He went up from Babylon, and he was a swift scribe in the law of Moses, which the Lord, the God of Israel, gave; and the king gave to him, because the hand of his God was upon him in everything that he sought.
verses.7:7: And some of the sons of Israel, and of the priests, and of the Levites, and the singers, and the gatekeepers, and the Nethinim went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes.
verses.7:8: And they came to Jerusalem in the fifth month; this was the seventh year of the king.
verses.7:9: For on the first day of the fifth month they came to Jerusalem, because the hand of his God was good upon him.
verses.7:10: For Ezra had set in his heart to seek the law, and to do and to teach statutes and judgment in Israel.
verses.7:11: And this is the copy of the edict that Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe of the book of the words of the commandments of the Lord and of His statutes over Israel:
verses.7:12: "Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra, scribe of the law of the God of heaven. The word and the answer had been completed.
verses.7:13: A decree has been issued by me that everyone in my kingdom from the people of Israel and the priests and the Levites who is willing to go to Jerusalem may go with you.
verses.7:14: From the presence of the king and the seven counselors, he was sent to inspect Judea and Jerusalem by the law of their God that is in your hand,
verses.7:15: and for the house of the Lord, silver and gold that the king and the counselors have freely offered to the Lord of Israel, who dwells in Jerusalem,
verses.7:16: and all the silver and gold that you may find in all the province of Babylon, with the freewill offering of the people and the priests who freely offer for the house of God that is in Jerusalem;
verses.7:17: and everything that comes in, promptly enter this in this book: young bulls, rams, lambs, and their sacrifices and their drink offerings; and you will offer them upon the altar of the house of your God that is in Jerusalem.
verses.7:18: And further, did it seem good to you and your brothers to act with the rest of the silver and the gold? Do as is pleasing to your God.
verses.7:19: And the vessels that are given to you for the service of the house of God, deliver before God in Jerusalem.
verses.7:20: And the rest of the need of the house of God, whatever seems good to you to give, you will give from the treasury houses of the king.
verses.7:21: And from me, I myself, King Artaxerxes, have issued a decree to all the treasuries that are beyond the River, that everything that Ezra the priest, scribe of the law of the God of heaven, asks of you, let it be done promptly,
verses.7:22: up to talents of silver, and up to one hundred kors of wheat, and up to one hundred storehouses of wine, and salt for which there is no written record.
verses.7:23: Everything that is in the decree of the God of heaven, let it be done. Take care not to attempt anything against the house of the God of heaven, so that wrath may not come upon the kingdom of the king and of his sons.
verses.7:24: And it has been made known to you concerning all the priests and the Levites, singers, gatekeepers, Nethinim, and ministers of this house of God: let there be no tribute for you; you will not have authority to enslave them.
verses.7:25: And you, Ezra, who have the wisdom of God in your hand, appoint scribes and judges, so that they may be judging all the people who are beyond the River, all those who know the law of God; and to the one who does not know, you will make it known.
verses.7:26: And everyone who is not promptly doing the law of God and the law of the king, judgment will be executed upon him, whether for death, or for discipline, or for forfeiture of property, or for custody."
verses.7:27: Blessed be the Lord, the God of our fathers, who put it thus into the heart of the king, who glorified the house that is in Jerusalem,
verses.7:28: and upon me He extended mercy in the eyes of the king and of his counselors and of all the exalted leaders of the king. And I was strengthened, as the good hand of God was upon me, and I gathered leaders from Israel to go up with me.
verses.8:1: And these are the leaders of their ancestral families, the guides going up with me in the reign of Artaxerxes, the king of Babylon:
verses.8:2: From the sons of Phinehas, Gershom; from the sons of Ithamar, Daniel; from the sons of David, Tous;
verses.8:3: from the sons of Shecaniah, from the sons of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him the company of one hundred and fifty;
verses.8:4: from the sons of Pahath-moab, Eliana the son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred males;
verses.8:5: and from the sons of Zattu, Shecaniah the son of Aziel, and with him three hundred males;
verses.8:6: and from the sons of Adin, Ebed the son of Jonathan, and with him fifty males;
verses.8:7: and from the sons of Elah, Jeshaiah the son of Athaliah, and with him seventy males;
verses.8:8: and from the sons of Shephatiah, Zebadiah the son of Michael, and with him eighty males;
verses.8:9: and from the sons of Joab, Adaiah the son of Jema, and with him two hundred and eighteen males;
verses.8:10: and from the sons of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah, and with him one hundred and sixty males;
verses.8:11: and from the sons of Bebai, also Azariah the son of Bebai, and with him seventy-eight males;
verses.8:12: and from the sons of Azgad, Johanan the son of Hakkatan, and with him one hundred and ten males;
verses.8:13: and from the sons of Adonikam, the last ones, and these are their names: Eliphelet and Euia and Shemaiah, sixty males;
verses.8:14: and from the sons of Bigvai, Uthai, and with him eighty males.
verses.8:15: And I gathered them to the river that comes to Euim, and we camped there three days. And I observed among the people and among the priests, and from the sons of Levi I did not find any there.
verses.8:16: And I sent for Eleazar, Ariel, Shemaiah, Alonam, Areb, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam, men; and for Areib and Elnathan, men of understanding.
verses.8:17: And I brought them out before a leader in the silver of the place, and I put words in their mouth to speak to their brothers of the Athanim in the silver of the place, to bring us singers for the house of our God.
verses.8:18: And there came to us, as the good hand of our God was upon us, a man, Sachoch, from the sons of Mahli, the son of Levi, the son of Israel; and at the beginning his sons and his brothers came, eighteen;
verses.8:19: and Hashabiah and Hoshaiah from the sons of Merari, his brothers and their sons, twenty;
verses.8:20: and from the Nethinim, whom David and the leaders gave for the service of the Levites, two hundred and twenty Nethinim; all of them were gathered by name.
verses.8:21: And I proclaimed a fast there at the river Thue, to humble ourselves before our God, to seek from Him a straight way for us and for our children and for all our possessions.
verses.8:22: For I was ashamed to ask from the king a force and horsemen to save us from an enemy on the way, because we had spoken to the king, saying, "The hand of our God is upon all those who seek Him for good, and His power and His wrath are upon all who forsake Him."
verses.8:23: And we fasted and sought from our God concerning this, and He listened to us.
verses.8:24: And I set apart twelve from the leaders of the priests, Seraiah, Hashabiah, and with them twelve from their brothers.
verses.8:25: And I weighed out to them the silver and the gold and the vessels of the offering of the house of our God, which the king and his counselors and his leaders and all Israel who were present had offered up.
verses.8:26: And I weighed out into their hands six hundred and fifty talents of silver, and one hundred silver vessels, and one hundred talents of gold,
verses.8:27: and twenty gold kaphudeth, for the way one thousand chamanim, and choice vessels of good gleaming bronze, desirable in gold.
verses.8:28: And I said to them, "You are holy to the Lord, and the vessels are holy, and the silver and the gold are freewill offerings to the Lord God of our fathers.
verses.8:29: Keep watch and guard them until you stand before the leaders of the priests and the Levites and the leaders of the ancestral families in Jerusalem, in the tents of the house of the Lord."
verses.8:30: And the priests and the Levites received the weight of the silver and the gold and the vessels, to bring them to Jerusalem, to the house of our God.
verses.8:31: And we departed from the river Thue on the twelfth day of the first month to go to Jerusalem; and the hand of our God was upon us, and He delivered us from the hand of an enemy and a foe on the way.
verses.8:32: And we came to Jerusalem, and we remained there three days.
verses.8:33: And it happened on the fourth day that we weighed out the silver and the gold and the vessels in the house of our God into the hand of Meremoth the son of Uriah the priest, and with him was Eleazar the son of Phinehas, and with them were Jozabad the son of Jeshua and Noadiah from Ebannaia, the Levites;
verses.8:34: everything by number and by weight, and all the weight was written down.
verses.8:35: At that time those who had come out of captivity, the sons of the exile, offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve young bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, twelve male goats for a sin offering, all of them as burnt offerings.
verses.8:36: And they delivered the decree of the king to the administrators of the king and to the governors beyond the River; and they honored the people and the house of God.
verses.9:1: And when these things were completed, the leaders approached me, saying, "The people of Israel and the priests and the Levites have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands in their abominations: the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite, the Ammonite, Moab, the Egyptian, and the Amorite;
verses.9:2: for they have taken some of their daughters for themselves and for their sons, and the holy seed has been led aside among the peoples of the lands, and the hand of the leaders is in this unfaithfulness."
verses.9:3: And when I heard this word, I tore my garments and trembled, and I pulled out some of the hair of my head and of my beard, and I sat still.
verses.9:4: And everyone who pursued the word of the God of Israel gathered to me over the unfaithfulness of the exile; and I was sitting still until the evening sacrifice.
verses.9:5: And at the evening sacrifice I rose from my humiliation; and as I tore my garments, I trembled, and I bowed down on my knees and spread out my hands to God,
verses.9:6: and I said, "I am ashamed and humiliated to lift up my face to You, for our iniquities have been multiplied above our head, and our transgressions have grown great up to heaven.
verses.9:7: From the days of our fathers we have been in great transgression until this day; and in our iniquities we and our kings and our sons have been handed over into the hand of the kings of the nations, to the sword and to captivity, to plunder and to shame of our face, as it is this day.
verses.9:8: And now our God has made provision for us to leave us for deliverance and to give us a firm hold in the place of His sanctuary, to enlighten our eyes and to give a little reviving in our bondage.
verses.9:9: For we are slaves, and in our bondage the Lord our God did not forsake us, and He extended mercy to us before the kings of Persia, to give us reviving, that they might raise up the house of our God and restore its ruins, and to give us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem.
verses.9:10: What shall we say, our God, after this? For we have forsaken Your commandments,
verses.9:11: which You gave to us by the hand of Your servants the prophets: 'The land into which you are entering to inherit it is a shifting land in the shifting of the peoples of the nations, in their abominations, with which they have filled it from mouth to mouth in their impurities.
verses.9:12: And now do not give your daughters to their sons, and do not take any of their daughters for your sons, and you shall not seek their peace and their good forever, so that you may grow strong and eat the good things of the land and leave it as an inheritance to your sons forever.'
verses.9:13: And after all that has come upon you in your evil deeds and in your great transgression, for there is none like our God, because You have lightened our iniquities and have given us deliverance,
verses.9:14: that we have turned back to break Your commandments and to intermarry with the peoples; do not be provoked to anger with us to complete destruction, so that there would be no remnant and no survivor.
verses.9:15: Lord God of Israel, You are righteous, for we have been left as survivors, as it is this day; we are before You in our transgressions, for it is not possible to stand before You because of this."
verses.10:1: And when Ezra prayed, and when he spoke out, weeping and praying before the house of God, a very large assembly gathered to him from Israel, men and women and youths; for the people wept and raised their weeping high.
verses.10:2: And Shecaniah son of Jehiel, from the sons of Elam, answered and said to Ezra, "We acted unfaithfully toward our God and married foreign wives from the peoples of the land; yet now there is hope for Israel concerning this.
verses.10:3: And now let us make a covenant with our God to cast out all the wives and those born from them, as you wish; arise and frighten them with the commandments of our God, and let it be done according to the law.
verses.10:4: Arise, for the matter is upon you, and we are with you; be strong and act."
verses.10:5: And Ezra arose and made the leaders, the Levites, and all Israel swear to act according to this word; and they swore.
verses.10:6: And Ezra arose from before the house of God and went into the treasury of Johanan son of Eliashib, and he went there; he ate no bread and drank no water, for he was mourning over the unfaithfulness of the exile.
verses.10:7: And they sent out a proclamation to Judah and in Jerusalem:
verses.10:8: "Everyone who does not come within three days, according to the counsel of the leaders and the elders, will have all his property placed under the ban, and he himself will be separated from the assembly of the exile."
verses.10:9: And all the men of Judah and Benjamin gathered to Jerusalem within the three days; this was the ninth month. On the twentieth day of the month, all the people sat in the open square of the house of God, because of their agitation concerning the matter and because of the storm.
verses.10:10: And Ezra the priest arose and said to them, "You have acted unfaithfully and married foreign wives, to add to the guilt of Israel.
verses.10:11: And now give praise to the God of our fathers, and do what is pleasing before Him, and separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from the foreign wives."
verses.10:12: And all the assembly answered and said, "Great is this word of yours for us to do.
verses.10:13: But the people are many, and the place is wintry, and there is no strength to stand outside; and the work is not for one day nor for two, for we have multiplied wrongdoing in this matter.
verses.10:14: Now let our leaders stand; and as for all those in our cities who married foreign wives, let them come at due times from the congregations, and with them the elders of each city and judges, to turn away the fierce wrath of our God from us concerning this matter."
verses.10:15: Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Lazeia son of Helkiah were with me concerning this, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite were helping them.
verses.10:16: And the sons of the exile did so; and Ezra the priest and men, leaders of ancestral houses, were set apart by house and all by name, for they returned on a day of the tenth month to investigate the matter.
verses.10:17: And they finished with all the men who had married foreign wives by the first day of the first month.
verses.10:18: And among the sons of the priests there were found those who had married foreign wives: from the sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers, Meessel and Eliezer and Jarim and Gedaliah;
verses.10:19: and they gave their hand to send out their wives, and a guilt-offering ram from the flock for their offense;
verses.10:20: and from the sons of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah;
verses.10:21: and from the sons of Harim: Masael and Elijah and Shemaiah and Jehiel and Uzziah;
verses.10:22: and from the sons of Pashhur: Eliona, Maaseiah and Samael and Nethanel and Jozabad and Elasah;
verses.10:23: and from the Levites: Jozabad and Samu and Kelaiah, that is, Kolieu, and Pedaiah and Jodom and Eliezer,
verses.10:24: and from the singers: Elisaph; and from the gatekeepers: Gellem and Telem and Oduth;
verses.10:25: and from Israel, from the sons of Parosh: Ramiah and Aziah and Malchijah and Amamin and Eleazar and Benaiah;
verses.10:26: and from the sons of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah and Jehiel and Abdiah and Jeremoth and Elijah;
verses.10:27: and from the sons of Zathuia: Eliona, Eliashib, Alathaniah and Amon and Zabadab and Uzziah;
verses.10:28: and from the sons of Bebai: Johanan, Niana and Zabu, Thali;
verses.10:29: and from the sons of Binnui: Melusam, Alum, Ada, Jasud and Saluia and Memon;
verses.10:30: and from the sons of Pahath-moab: Aidaine, Chael, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel and Thanui and Manasseh;
verses.10:31: and from the sons of Harim: Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Simeon,
verses.10:33: From the sons of Hashum: Mattaniah, Atha, Zabel, Eliphaneth, Jeramim, Manasseh, Shimei;
verses.10:34: from the sons of Ani: Modediah, Mari, Uel,
verses.10:38: The sons of Binnui and the sons of Shimei,
verses.10:39: and Shelemiah and Nathan and Adaiah,
verses.10:43: from the sons of Nebo: Jeiel, Thamathiah, Sedem, Zanbina, Dia and Joel and Benaiah.
verses.10:44: All these took foreign wives, and they fathered sons by them.

notes.1:1: This Greek text lacks "the word of the Lord" and "the Lord" here (as well as "the Lord" in vv. 2, 5, and 7, and the closing clause of v. 3), leaving "to be fulfilled" without an explicit noun and "He roused" with an implied divine subject (compare v. 5).
notes.1:2: Greek epeskepsato me ep' eme (literally "visited/charged me upon me") doubles the pronominal object, reflecting the Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew idiom for appointing or commissioning; the verse also reads "all the kingdoms" without "of the earth".
notes.1:8: Greek Tasbarenou (a textual variant for Gasbarenou) transliterates the Persian title for "treasurer" (Hebrew haggizbar) as a proper name, and Greek Sabanasar corresponds to Hebrew Sheshbazzar.
notes.1:9: Greek Kyrio ("for the Lord") appears where other Septuagint witnesses read psyktēres ("basins/coolers"), leaving the adjectives "gold" and "silver" without a noun; paregmena (literally "things passed along/altered") renders an obscure Hebrew term often understood as "knives" or "censers".
notes.1:10: Greek kepphoures transliterates the Hebrew vessel term keporim ("bowls" or "covered bowls"); this Greek text also reads "six" silver bowls (rather than "four hundred and ten" in the Hebrew Masoretic Text) and omits Sheshbazzar/Sabanasar in v. 11.
notes.2:2: The Greek text preserves several distinctive leader names compared to the Hebrew Masoretic Text (Araiah for Seraiah, Marathchai for Mordecai, Baspham for Bilshan, Malsar for Mispar, Batusi for Bigvai, and Balleia for Baanah) and omits Rehum; it also reads 'the men of Israel' without 'the people.'
notes.2:4: The Greek reads 'Asaph' with 472 (MT reads 'Shephatiah' with 372); similarly, 2:3 reads 'Perez' (MT 'Parosh'), 2:5 reads 'Era' (MT 'Arah'), 2:6 reads 'Phalab-moab' and 'Jobab' (MT 'Pahath-moab' and 'Joab'), and 2:7 reads 'Malam' (MT 'Elam').
notes.2:12: The Greek gives 3,222 (MT reads 1,222), and 2:16 reads 92 (MT 98). Distinctive Greek name forms also appear in 2:9-10, 14, 17-18, and 20-21 (Zacchu, Banu, Baogei, Basu, Ura, Taber, and Barthaleem for MT Zaccai, Bani, Bigvai, Bezai, Jorah, Gibbar, and Bethlehem).
notes.2:31: The Greek fuses the Hebrew phrase for 'the other Elam' into a single proper name, 'Elamar,' and reads 2,254 (MT reads 1,254); similarly, 2:26 reads 'Haram' (MT 'Ramah') and 2:28 reads 'Gaithel' (MT 'Bethel').
notes.2:33: The Greek reads 'Haroth' and 625 (MT reads 'Hadid' and 725); in 2:34 the Greek likewise reads 'Jereia' where MT reads 'Jericho.'
notes.2:43: The Greek transliterates Hebrew 'Nethinim' (temple servants; spelled 'Thanieim' in 2:70) and preserves several distinctive names across 2:36-57 (including Jeuda, Soduiah, Akum, Abau, Suthia, Kadesh, Soel, Akaboth, Samaan, Keded, Gael, Reel, Phison, Manoemin, Naphison, Haphika, Basadoe, Mauda, Nasus, Phadura, Gedea, Hateia, Phasrath, and Haseboin), while omitting Sisera in 2:53. In 2:39 and 2:41 the Greek counts 1,007 and 148 (MT reads 1,017 and 128).
notes.2:55: The Greek transliterates the Hebrew title 'servants of Solomon' as proper names: 'Abdesel' here and 'Asedeselma' in 2:58. In 2:58 the Greek numeral gives 372 (MT reads 392).
notes.2:62: 'Methoesim' transliterates the Hebrew participle for 'those enrolled by genealogy,' and 'excluded' renders a Greek verb literally meaning 'be treated as next of kin,' reflecting the Hebrew homonym for 'be defiled/excluded.' Distinctive Greek names also appear in 2:59-61, including the extra clan 'Bua' in 2:60 and 'Zarbelthei' alongside 'Barzillai' in 2:61.
notes.2:63: 'Hathersaa' transliterates the Persian title for 'the governor' (Tirshatha). 'The lights and the perfections' translates the Greek rendering of Hebrew Urim and Thummim.
notes.2:65: The Greek reads 7,334 (MT 7,337) and literally 'singers and songs' (MT 'male and female singers'). Distinctive Greek figures also appear in 2:66 (730 horses; MT 736), 2:67 (720 donkeys; MT 6,720), and 2:69 (61,000 minas of pure gold; MT 61,000 gold darics).
notes.3:2: The Greek text omits "the priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and his brothers," which appear in the Hebrew text.
notes.3:3: The Greek text omits the clause about dread of the peoples of the lands found in the Hebrew text and uses an intransitive singular verb ("a burnt offering went up").
notes.3:7: Greek Sedamein and Sorein transliterate the Hebrew terms corresponding to the Sidonians and Tyrians.
notes.3:10: The Greek text reads "laid the foundation to build" (taking the Hebrew participle for "builders" as an infinitive) and omits "with cymbals."
notes.3:11: The Greek text reads neuter agathon ("it is good") rather than masculine ("He is good"); similarly in v. 12 it reads "a song" (oden) where the Hebrew has "the voice."
notes.4:6: Greek Astherou is a distinct textual form corresponding to Ahasuerus in the Hebrew text; the Greek also reads singular "he wrote" and omits "an accusation."
notes.4:7: The Greek text spells Artaxerxes as Asarthatha here (and Arsartha in vv. 8, 11, 23), translates the Hebrew proper name Bishlam as "in peace," and renders the Persian loanword for "letter" as "the tax collector" (ho phorologos, also in vv. 18, 23; 5:5).
notes.4:8: Greek Raoul Badatamen (and Rehum Baal in v. 9, Rehum Balgam in v. 17) transliterates the Aramaic title for "commander/chancellor" rather than translating it; the Greek also spells Shimshai variously across the chapter and reads "who are Elamites" in v. 9 where the Aramaic lists the Dehavites.
notes.4:12: The Greek text reads "from Cyrus" (apo Kyrou) where the Aramaic has "from you," and in v. 14 omits the clause about eating the salt of the palace.
notes.4:15: Greek phygadeia doulon ("places of refuge for slaves") reflects a different reading of the Aramaic phrase for "stirring up sedition" (similarly in v. 19); in v. 17 Greek phasin is read as the noun "statement" rather than a verb.
notes.5:3: Greek choregia ("outfitting" or "equipment," also in v. 9) translates a rare Aramaic architectural term for structure or wall; v. 9 also omits "this house."
notes.5:4: The Greek text reads third-person "they said" and "this city" where the Aramaic text has "we said" and "this building."
notes.5:5: Greek ten aichmalosin Iouda ("the captivity of Judah") reflects reading the Aramaic consonantal text for "elders of the Jews" as "captivity."
notes.5:14: Greek Bagasar (and Sarbagar in v. 16) are distinct Greek forms corresponding to Sheshbazzar in the Aramaic text, and the Greek describes him as "the treasurer, who was over the treasury" rather than "governor."
notes.5:17: The Greek text reads "so that you may know that" (rather than "whether") and "when the king knows" (gnous) where the Aramaic has "the king's pleasure."
notes.6:2: The Greek reads simply "in the city, in the citadel," omitting the names of Ecbatana and the province of Media found in the Aramaic Masoretic Text.
notes.6:6: The Greek reads "you will give" (dosete), apparently interpreting the Aramaic name Tattenai (which appears as Tanthanai in 6:13) as a verb meaning "to give," and also uses plural "governors" and "their fellow servants."
notes.6:8: The Greek reads "that you never do anything" (me pote ti poiesete), taking the Aramaic clause ("concerning what you shall do") as a prohibition.
notes.6:11: The Greek phrase "what belongs to me" (to kat' eme) indicates confiscation to the crown, contrasting with the Aramaic Masoretic Text's "a refuse heap."
notes.6:21: The Greek omits "who had returned" before "from the exile" and reads "with regard to the impurities" (eis akatharsias, literally "into/regarding the impurities") rather than "from the impurity."
notes.7:3: The Greek genealogy reads the distinct name "Samariah" (Samareia) here, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Amariah."
notes.7:4: The Greek genealogy reads the distinct name "Saouia" here, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Uzzi."
notes.7:9: The Greek omits the clause concerning Ezra's departure from Babylon on the first day of the first month (found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text) and uses plural "they came" here and in 7:8.
notes.7:17: The Greek reads "everything that comes in, promptly enter this in this book" (apparently reading Aramaic "book" for "silver"), contrasting with the Aramaic Masoretic Text's instruction to "diligently buy with this silver."
notes.7:22: The Greek lacks the numeral "one hundred" before "talents of silver," omits oil from the list, and renders "baths" of wine as "storehouses" (apothekon).
notes.8:1: The Greek reads 'the guides going up with me' and 'the king of Babylon,' where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'the genealogy of those who went up with me' and 'from Babylon.'
notes.8:5: The Greek preserves the ancestral family of Zattu (absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text here). Across the 8:2-14 roster, the Greek also preserves several distinct names and numbers compared with the Hebrew text: Tous (8:2, for Hattush), Eliana (8:4, for Eliehoenai), Aziel (8:5, for Jahaziel), Elah (8:7, for Elam), Adaiah and Jema (8:9, for Obadiah and Jehiel), Azariah and seventy-eight (8:11, for Zechariah and twenty-eight), Euia (8:13, for Jeiel), and eighty (8:14, for seventy).
notes.8:15: The Greek names the river destination Euim here and Thue in 8:21 and 8:31, where the Hebrew text reads Ahava. In 8:16 the Greek also reads Eleazar, Alonam, Areb, and Areib (for Hebrew Eliezer, Elnathan, Jarib, and Joiarib), and in 8:24 and 8:33 it reads Seraiah (with twelve brothers) and 'from Ebannaia' (for Sherebiah with ten, and 'son of Binnui').
notes.8:17: The Greek renders the place-name Casiphia as 'in the silver of the place' (from the Aramaic/Hebrew root for silver), reads Athanim (a variant of Nethinim, cf. 8:20), and has 'singers' rather than 'ministers.' In 8:18-19 'Sachoch' is an untranslated transliteration of Hebrew sekel ('discretion'), 'at the beginning' replaces Sherebiah, and Hoshaiah appears for Jeshaiah.
notes.8:27: Both 'kaphudeth' and 'chamanim' are untranslated Greek transliterations corresponding to Hebrew 'bowls' and 'darics,' with the first part of 'darics' interpreted as 'for the way.' The adjective 'choice' translates Greek diaphora ('distinct/choice') where the Hebrew text reads 'two.'
notes.9:1: The rare Greek noun makrymma (literally 'something put far away,' also in 9:11) renders Hebrew 'abominations,' and 'the Egyptian' translates the Greek transliteration Moserei (from Hebrew Mitsri). In 9:2 the Greek reads 'has been led aside' (parechthe) rather than 'has mingled.'
notes.9:3: Here and in 9:5 the Greek reads 'and trembled' (epallomen) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'and my robe.' In 9:4 'everyone who pursued the word' renders Greek diokon logon (versus Hebrew 'trembled at the words').
notes.9:8: The Greek reads 'has made provision for us' (epeskeuasato, likely an early Greek variant for epieikeusato, 'dealt graciously'), differing from the Hebrew text's 'for a brief moment favor has been shown.' In 9:7 the Greek reads 'our sons' rather than 'our priests.'
notes.9:11: 'A shifting land in the shifting of the peoples of the nations' renders Greek metakinoumene ... en metakinesei, connecting Hebrew niddah ('impurity') to the root for moving or shifting. 'From mouth to mouth' literally preserves a Hebrew idiom meaning 'from end to end.'
notes.9:13: The Greek shifts briefly to second-person plural ('you,' 'your') before returning to first-person plural, and reads 'for there is none like our God, because You have lightened our iniquities.' In 9:14 the Greek frames the confession as a statement followed by a plea ('do not be provoked to anger') rather than rhetorical questions.
notes.10:2: The Greek verb translated "married" (here and in vv. 10, 14, 17, 18) literally means "settled," rendering the Hebrew idiom for bringing women into one's household as wives.
notes.10:3: The Greek text reads "as you wish; arise and frighten them with the commandments of our God," diverging notably from the Hebrew ("according to the counsel of my lord and of those who tremble at the commandment of our God").
notes.10:7: Translated verbatim from the Greek text, which lacks the clause "to all the returned exiles to assemble at Jerusalem" found in the Hebrew, likely through scribal eye-skip between the two occurrences of "Jerusalem."
notes.10:15: The Greek reads "were with me concerning this" (contrast Hebrew "opposed this") and preserves the LXX-distinct names Lazeia son of Helkiah (Hebrew: Jahzeiah son of Tikvah).
notes.10:37: The Greek renders the final Hebrew name (Jaasu/Jaasai) as a verb, "and they acted." Throughout vv. 18-43, numerous LXX-distinct personal names (such as Meessel, Jarim, Masael, Eliona, Samael, Samu, Kolieu, Jodom, Elisaph, Gellem, Oduth, Amamin, Alathaniah, Amon, Zabadab, Niana, Melusam, Alum, Memon, Chael, Thanui, Baluch, Atha, Zabel, Eliphaneth, Ani, Modediah, Mari, Baraiah, Hilkiah, Mathanan, Machadnabu, Sariu, Mariah, Thamathiah, Sedem, and Dia) are retained faithfully from the Greek text.
